1→# Identity probe

Grill settled 2026-08-28. ADR 0011. Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` (Identity pass — Sign-up, API auth, Connected, Probe, Config, Reader, Runner). Session still means an agent transcript. Do not say login session.

Seams (please confirm): **one Probe HTTP contract on doraval.dev** (login callback, key mint, hello / status / ack) + **existing spawn-CLI and Config** (store the key, one Probe command that waits). No third seam. The site is the store. The CLI is a client. Do not add a local UI.

## Problem Statement

A Reader cannot tell that the CLI and doraval.dev can talk. There is no account. There is no API key. The site is static docs. The next identity work (Config UI, Config sync) has nothing to hang on. A fake “logged in” switch would teach a dead end. Uploading Config now would put Judge secrets on the site before we have a rule.
10→
## Solution

This pass proves a logged-in two-way loop. Nothing else.

A visitor on doraval.dev sees login, not Config. Sign-up and login are Scalekit OAuth (SaaSKit). The callback lives on doraval.dev. Docs pages stay public.

A logged-in Reader mints an API key once, copies it, and stores it in Config with `dora config`. That is Connected.

One CLI command sends **hello**, waits, and prints **ack** when the Reader clicks ack on the site. The UI shows hello. Config stays on the machine. The UI does not write Config.
20→
The site gains a server: Blume `output: "server"` plus the Netlify adapter. Trusted from Blume docs. Not proven by a prior deploy. Docs pages stay prerendered.

## User Stories

1. As a visitor, I want public docs without an account, so that I can still read doraval.dev.
2. As a visitor, I want the Probe and Config UI hidden behind login, so that I do not see an empty editor.
3. As a visitor, I want a login control, so that I know how to start Sign-up.
4. As a Reader, I want Sign-up via Scalekit’s hosted page, so that I do not invent a password form.
5. As a Reader, I want login via the same hosted page, so that Sign-up and login are one product.
30→6. As a Reader, I want the callback on doraval.dev, so that I land back on the site after Scalekit.
7. As a Reader, I want logout, so that a shared browser is not left signed in.
8. As a Runner, I want login and logout to be human actions, so that I do not automate a browser Sign-up.
9. As a Reader, I want a minted API key shown once, so that I can put it in the CLI.
10. As a Reader, I want the site to refuse to show that key again, so that a later visit is not a leak.
11. As a Reader, I want to store the key with `dora config`, so that I do not learn a second settings file.
12. As a Reader, I want that key stored as a secret next to Judge keys, so that `dora config` list does not print it.
13. As a Runner, I want `dora config set` of that key to need `--yes` or `--dry-run`, so that I do not hang and I do not write by accident.
14. As a Reader, I want Connected to mean “this CLI has a valid key,” not “dora is on PATH.”
15. As a Reader, I want the site to say not Connected until a Probe arrives with a valid key, so that I see the same fact as the CLI.
40→16. As a Runner, I want a Probe without a key to exit `2` with Next to set the key, so that I can recover.
17. As a Reader, I want one Probe command that sends hello and waits, so that the proof is one invoke.
18. As a Runner, I want that command to support `--json`, so that I can branch on hello vs ack vs timeout.
19. As a Runner, I want `--dry-run` on the Probe to print the plan and call nothing, so that I can preview.
20. As a detected agent, I want a Probe without `--yes` or `--dry-run` to exit `2` and write nothing, so that I follow the write gate.
21. As a Reader, I want the UI to show hello after the CLI sends it, so that I see the CLI reached the site.
22. As a Reader, I want an ack control on that hello, so that I complete the loop.
23. As a Reader, I want the waiting CLI to print ack and exit `0` after I click, so that I know two-way worked.
24. As a Reader, I want a timeout if I never ack, so that the CLI does not hang forever.
25. As a Runner, I want a timeout to exit `1` with Next, so that I am not told it succeeded.
50→26. As a Reader, I want a bad or revoked key to fail the Probe, so that I am not shown another account’s hello.
27. As a Reader, I want hello to be a fixed probe payload, so that Config never leaves the machine this pass.
28. As a Reader, I want ack to write nothing to Config, so that the UI cannot change `config.yml`.
29. As a Reader, I want a second Probe to be its own hello, so that an old ack cannot close a new wait.
30. As a logged-in Reader without a key, I want Next that tells me to mint a key, so that I am not stuck on an empty Probe page.
31. As a Reader, I want `--help` for the Probe command to talk to the Runner, so that help matches ADR 0001.
32. As a Reader, I want `dora --help` and `--help --json` to list the Probe command as a write, so that the map is not stale.
33. As a Reader, I want docs lockstep only if a new help line would otherwise lie, so that this is not a docs rewrite.
34. As a founder, I want no version bump unless I ask, so that this is not a release.
35. As a Reader, I want the Scalekit client secret only on the server, so that the static HTML does not hold it.
60→36. As a Reader, I want missing Scalekit env on the server to fail login with a clear error, so that I do not get a blank callback.
37. As a Reader, I want existing docs routes to keep working after the site is no longer static-only, so that get-started does not break.
38. As a Reader, I want prerendered docs pages to stay prerendered, so that the catalog does not need a server hit.
39. As an implementer, I want Blume server output plus the Netlify adapter, so that we follow Blume’s documented path.
40. As an implementer, I want the Probe store on the server, so that a static page is not asked to remember hello.
41. As a Reader, I want login not to be called a Session, so that Session still means an agent transcript.
42. As a Reader, I want MCP OAuth and AgentKit left unused, so that this pass is SaaSKit plus API keys only.
43. As a CI job, I want Probe HTTP tests to use a fake Scalekit, so that CI does not call the real dashboard.
44. As a Reader, I want to revoke or rotate a key later without this pass inventing a key list UI, so that v1 stays the mint-once proof.
45. As a Reader, I want Coming soon unused for the Probe itself, so that the loop is real, not a stub.
70→46. As a Runner, I want unknown Probe flags to fail like other verbs, so that I get Next, not a hang.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Glossary.** Use Identity-pass terms only. Session is never a login. Connected is a valid API key in Config, not install detection.
- **ADR 0011.** Config UI and Config sync stay later. This pass is the Probe only. Server lives on doraval.dev.
- **Seams.** One Probe HTTP contract (site). Existing Config + spawn-CLI (key + one waiting command). No local UI. No third planner unless the HTTP contract needs a tiny client helper that the CLI already uses for other HTTP.
- **Scalekit products.** SaaSKit hosted login for humans. Scalekit API keys (`createToken` / `validateToken`) for the CLI. Not AgentKit. Not MCP OAuth. Not M2M client-credentials JWT as the customer key (the customer holds a long-lived API key).
- **Login.** Authorization code. Server exchanges the code. Client secret stays on the server. Env names: `SCALEKIT_ENVIRONMENT_URL`, `SCALEKIT_CLIENT_ID`, `SCALEKIT_CLIENT_SECRET`. Callback URL registered in the Scalekit dashboard. Missing env: login fails, docs still serve.
- **Docs stay public.** Only Probe, key mint, and account controls require login. Visitor sees login, not Config, not hello.
80→- **API key.** Logged-in mint, show once, store `tokenId` server-side if needed for validate. Reader pastes the token into Config as a secret key. Never push the key back to the site. Never log the token.
- **Config key.** One new secret key on the existing Config catalog, same secret treatment as the Judge key. `dora config get/set/list` work. List redacts it.
- **Probe command.** One noun-style write under the existing CLI tree (help talks to the Runner). Sends hello, polls status, prints ack or times out. `--json`, `--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--ci` as on other writes. Default timeout is short enough for a human click (minutes, not hours).
- **Probe payload.** Fixed hello and ack strings. No Config. No Skill list. No Session data.
- **HTTP contract (site).** Authenticated CLI (bearer API key): create hello, read status. Authenticated browser: view latest hello, post ack. Validate the key on every CLI request. A new hello does not complete from an old ack.
- **Site server.** Blume server output + Netlify adapter. Install the Netlify adapter package. Docs routes stay prerendered. Add only the live routes this pass needs. Trust Blume deployment docs; first deploy is the proof.
- **Write gate.** Detected agent without `--yes` / `--dry-run` on Config set and on Probe: exit `2`, no network, no write. Human TTY may confirm.
- **Voice.** `--help` is Runner. README / get-started stay Reader. Lockstep only when a help line would disagree.
- **No version bump** unless the user asks for a release.

90→## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior only: HTTP status and JSON, CLI stdout/stderr, exit codes, Config file secret redaction, “docs URL still 200.” Do not test private helpers. Do not call live Scalekit in CI.
- **Probe HTTP tests:** create hello with a valid key; reject missing/bad key; status is pending then acked; old ack does not close a new hello; unauthenticated browser cannot ack.
- **Spawn-CLI tests:** Probe `--help`; write gate exit `2`; `--dry-run` sends nothing; `--yes` waits and reports; no key exit `2` with Next; timeout exit `1`; `--json` shape; `dora --help --json` lists the write.
- **Config tests:** new secret key sets, redacts on list, does not print on get in human mode the same way Judge keys already behave.
- **Site smoke:** public docs path still serves after server output is on.
- Prior art: Config secret tests, write-gate tests on fix / skill remove, spawn-CLI helper, `check-site` for docs artifacts.

## Out of Scope
100→
- Config UI and Config sync (parked; ADR 0011).
- Pushing Config or Judge secrets to the site.
- UI writes to `config.yml`.
- Coming-soon-only stub instead of a real Probe.
- Local-only UI as the destination.
- A second API host as the default.
- AgentKit, MCP OAuth, SCIM, SSO beyond hosted Sign-up/login.
- Key list / rotate / revoke UI (mint once is enough).
- Observability product.
110→- Library prune (#73).
- Memory overhaul.
- Version bump / npm publish.
- A typed SDK.

## Further Notes

Confirm the two seams before `/to-tickets`. If you want one seam only, drop CLI unit tests and drive Probe only through spawn-CLI plus HTTP tests against a test server; that is worse for the Config secret. Two is the right number.

Human step before implement: Scalekit dashboard app, callback URL, env on the Netlify site. Do not put secrets in the repo or in chat.
120→
Next: `/to-tickets`. Then `/implement` per ticket, clear between tickets.

# Identity probe

Seams (please confirm): **one Probe HTTP contract on doraval.dev** (login callback, key mint, hello / status / ack) + **existing spawn-CLI and Config** (store the key, one Probe command that waits). No third seam. The site is the store. The CLI is a client. Do not add a local UI.

## Problem Statement

A Reader cannot tell that the CLI and doraval.dev can talk. There is no account. There is no API key. The site is static docs. The next identity work (Config UI, Config sync) has nothing to hang on. A fake “logged in” switch would teach a dead end. Uploading Config now would put Judge secrets on the site before we have a rule.

## Solution

This pass proves a logged-in two-way loop. Nothing else.

A visitor on doraval.dev sees login, not Config. Sign-up and login are Scalekit OAuth (SaaSKit). The callback lives on doraval.dev. Docs pages stay public.

A logged-in Reader mints an API key once, copies it, and stores it in Config with `dora config`. That is Connected.

One CLI command sends **hello**, waits, and prints **ack** when the Reader clicks ack on the site. The UI shows hello. Config stays on the machine. The UI does not write Config.

1. As a visitor, I want public docs without an account, so that I can still read doraval.dev.
2. As a visitor, I want the Probe and Config UI hidden behind login, so that I do not see an empty editor.
3. As a visitor, I want a login control, so that I know how to start Sign-up.
4. As a Reader, I want Sign-up via Scalekit’s hosted page, so that I do not invent a password form.
5. As a Reader, I want login via the same hosted page, so that Sign-up and login are one product.
6. As a Reader, I want the callback on doraval.dev, so that I land back on the site after Scalekit.
7. As a Reader, I want logout, so that a shared browser is not left signed in.
8. As a Runner, I want login and logout to be human actions, so that I do not automate a browser Sign-up.
9. As a Reader, I want a minted API key shown once, so that I can put it in the CLI.
10. As a Reader, I want the site to refuse to show that key again, so that a later visit is not a leak.
11. As a Reader, I want to store the key with `dora config`, so that I do not learn a second settings file.
12. As a Reader, I want that key stored as a secret next to Judge keys, so that `dora config` list does not print it.
13. As a Runner, I want `dora config set` of that key to need `--yes` or `--dry-run`, so that I do not hang and I do not write by accident.
14. As a Reader, I want Connected to mean “this CLI has a valid key,” not “dora is on PATH.”
15. As a Reader, I want the site to say not Connected until a Probe arrives with a valid key, so that I see the same fact as the CLI.
16. As a Runner, I want a Probe without a key to exit `2` with Next to set the key, so that I can recover.
17. As a Reader, I want one Probe command that sends hello and waits, so that the proof is one invoke.
18. As a Runner, I want that command to support `--json`, so that I can branch on hello vs ack vs timeout.
19. As a Runner, I want `--dry-run` on the Probe to print the plan and call nothing, so that I can preview.
20. As a detected agent, I want a Probe without `--yes` or `--dry-run` to exit `2` and write nothing, so that I follow the write gate.
21. As a Reader, I want the UI to show hello after the CLI sends it, so that I see the CLI reached the site.
22. As a Reader, I want an ack control on that hello, so that I complete the loop.
23. As a Reader, I want the waiting CLI to print ack and exit `0` after I click, so that I know two-way worked.
24. As a Reader, I want a timeout if I never ack, so that the CLI does not hang forever.
25. As a Runner, I want a timeout to exit `1` with Next, so that I am not told it succeeded.
26. As a Reader, I want a bad or revoked key to fail the Probe, so that I am not shown another account’s hello.
27. As a Reader, I want hello to be a fixed probe payload, so that Config never leaves the machine this pass.
28. As a Reader, I want ack to write nothing to Config, so that the UI cannot change `config.yml`.
29. As a Reader, I want a second Probe to be its own hello, so that an old ack cannot close a new wait.
30. As a logged-in Reader without a key, I want Next that tells me to mint a key, so that I am not stuck on an empty Probe page.
31. As a Reader, I want `--help` for the Probe command to talk to the Runner, so that help matches ADR 0001.
32. As a Reader, I want `dora --help` and `--help --json` to list the Probe command as a write, so that the map is not stale.
33. As a Reader, I want docs lockstep only if a new help line would otherwise lie, so that this is not a docs rewrite.
34. As a founder, I want no version bump unless I ask, so that this is not a release.
35. As a Reader, I want the Scalekit client secret only on the server, so that the static HTML does not hold it.
36. As a Reader, I want missing Scalekit env on the server to fail login with a clear error, so that I do not get a blank callback.
37. As a Reader, I want existing docs routes to keep working after the site is no longer static-only, so that get-started does not break.
38. As a Reader, I want prerendered docs pages to stay prerendered, so that the catalog does not need a server hit.
39. As an implementer, I want Blume server output plus the Netlify adapter, so that we follow Blume’s documented path.
40. As an implementer, I want the Probe store on the server, so that a static page is not asked to remember hello.
41. As a Reader, I want login not to be called a Session, so that Session still means an agent transcript.
42. As a Reader, I want MCP OAuth and AgentKit left unused, so that this pass is SaaSKit plus API keys only.
43. As a CI job, I want Probe HTTP tests to use a fake Scalekit, so that CI does not call the real dashboard.
44. As a Reader, I want to revoke or rotate a key later without this pass inventing a key list UI, so that v1 stays the mint-once proof.

1→# dora verbs

Same order as `dora --help`. Flags: `dora <command> --help`. Map: `dora --help --json`.
Bare noun groups **list**. Create sits on the noun (`… new`).

| Command | Job |
| --- | --- |
| `dora` | Short `--help`. First job is `dora review --quick`. |
| `dora review [path]` | Gate: structure → heuristics → Judge → sessions. Full Review adds Session health. `--quick` skips Judge and Session health. |
10→| `dora fix [path]` | Mechanical `--yes`. Judgment `--brief` / `--json` (`message`, `severity`, `hint`, optional `code` / `docUrl`). |
| `dora scan` | Workspace map. Not the empty-argv default. |
| `dora skill` | List Authored + Global Skills |
| `dora skill unused` | Unused Skills. Remove candidates are never invoked and not a Recent install. `--global` is home Skills. `--last` / `--since` override the Review window for one run. |
| `dora skill remove` / `restore` | Delete Authored or Quarantine / restore Global |
| `dora skill new` | Scaffold a Skill |
| `dora rule` | List review rules |
| `dora rule new` | Scaffold a Rule |
| `dora session` | List Sessions. `show <id>` (short id is enough if unique) |
| `dora memory` | List principles. `add` / `promote` (`promote` writes `AGENTS.md`) |
20→| `dora conflicts` | Cross-agent contradictions (`--dry-run`, then `--yes`) |
| `dora config` | List keys. `get` / `set` / `setup` (Judge keys) |
| `dora agent` | List Subagents |
| `dora agent new` | Scaffold a Subagent |
| `dora plugin` | List Plugins |
| `dora plugin new` | Scaffold a Plugin |
| `dora plugin bump` | Plugin and marketplace semver |
| `dora update` | Update doraval |

Writes take `--yes` or `--dry-run`. Missing flag is **exit 2**.
